cards.title: What the test measures
cards.body: Radiated emissions are the electric field leaving the box and its cables. They are not the voltage on the mains. The number you compare with the limit is the maximized field, in the detector and at the distance the limit was written for.

cards.title: Distance
cards.body: Under Part 15 the distance is horizontal, to the closest point of the system boundary. Support gear and cables inside that boundary count. At and above 30 MHz, a different distance is moved with 20 dB/decade. Below 30 MHz the default factor is 40 dB/decade.

cards.title: Detectors
cards.body: On and below 1 GHz the Part 15 limits are quasi-peak. A peak detector with the same bandwidth may be used to pass, because peak does not read lower. Above 1 GHz the limit is an average limit, bandwidth at least 1 MHz, and the peak cap is generally 20 dB higher.

cards.title: The Class B shape
cards.body: Section 15.109(a) at 3 m is 100, 150, 200, and 500 µV/m across 30–88, 88–216, 216–960, and above 960 MHz. The tighter value applies at a band edge. Above 1 GHz that 500 µV/m figure is the average limit. At 980 MHz it is still quasi-peak.

cards.title: Class A is a 10 m table
cards.body: Section 15.109(b) is 90, 150, 210, and 300 µV/m at 10 m, in the same four bands. Do not paste those numbers onto a 3 m plot without the 20 dB/decade move. The worked example in §15.109(g)(2) turns 500 µV/m at 3 m into 150 µV/m at 10 m.

cards.title: ICES-003 is close, not identical
cards.body: Table 2 is quasi-peak from 30 MHz to 1 GHz. Class B at 3 m is 40.0, 43.5, 46.0, 47.0, and 54.0 dBµV/m in the five bands the table actually prints. The FCC 216–960 MHz cell is one number. ICES splits 216–230 from 230–960. Do not swap the tables.

cards.title: How far up the dial
cards.body: Section 15.33(b)(1) and ICES-003 Table 3 share the breakpoints: under 1.705 MHz stop at 30 MHz, then 1 GHz, 2 GHz, 5 GHz, and above 1 GHz go to five times the highest frequency, capped at 40 GHz. Satellite outdoor units under ICES-003 go to 18 GHz and also follow Annex H.

cards.title: Finding the maximum
cards.body: Use both polarizations, turn the product, and scan antenna height (commonly 1–4 m below 1 GHz). Exercise the noisiest intended mode. A prescan that never moves the table is a search, not a result. Table height below 1 GHz is commonly 0.8 m. Record the height your method actually requires above 1 GHz.

cards.title: Usual ways to get it wrong
cards.body: A missing antenna factor or cable loss makes the product look too quiet. A saturated preamp lies in the other direction. An ambient on the limit line is not a product reading. Calling a peak over the quasi-peak limit a quasi-peak failure, or a quasi-peak pass, skips the detector the limit is written in.

cards.title: Previews are not tables
cards.body: The IEC 61000-6-3 and CISPR 14-1 files in this pack are previews. They tell you the product family and that the tables exist. They do not print the numbers. ICES-003 has one limit set and allows either CISPR 32 or ANSI C63.4 as the method, not as a second limit.
